content.title: About
content.content: Full‑fat cream cheese in a block (5713) is a soft, high‑fat cheese made from pasteurised cow’s milk. It has a creamy texture, mild buttery flavor and is used as a base for desserts, sauces, fillings and spreads.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cream cheese is often called “cheese spread”, though production methods vary worldwide.
The full‑fat version contains about 33 % fat in dry matter, making it richer than reduced‑fat varieties.
Blocks are easy to slice and shape, simplifying culinary use.
In American cuisine it is a key ingredient for cheesecakes and dips.
In Russia it is sold under brands like “Slyvochnyi” or “Kremovyi”.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: Cream cheese provides calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains vitamins B2, B12 and niacin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Protein content
items.content: A serving delivers about 6 g of high‑quality milk protein for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Fatty acids
items.content: Full‑fat cheese supplies short‑ and medium‑chain fatty acids that are readily metabolised.

items.title: Probiotic cultures
items.content: Some cream cheeses are fermented, which may benefit gut microbiota.

items.title: High fat and calorie content
items.content: Full‑fat cream cheese is energy‑dense; portion control is advisable for weight management.

items.title: Lactose
items.content: Contains lactose, which can cause discomfort for lactose‑intolerant individuals.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to casein or whey may react to cream cheese.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Some brands add salt, which should be considered by those limiting sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cream cheese can be spread on bread, used in sandwich fillings, mixed into sauces, creams and desserts, or incorporated into baked goods. It blends well with herbs, spices or fruit purées for varied flavours.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the block in its original packaging or an airtight container in the refrigerator at +2‑+6 °C. Once opened, it is best used within 2‑3 weeks. Discard if it develops a sour smell or visible mold.
